title: Why people hate AI
author: Physical-Bite-3837
selftext:
Ever heard of Jacque Fresco?   
  
He was an American futurist and industrial designer who advocated for a resource-based economy. Essentially, he believed the monetary system (a system that uses money i.e. capitalism)  is the reason some people feared and hated technological advancement.  A machine that can do your job should mean less work for you, but when your livelihood depends on selling your labor, it becomes a threat instead.

He died before the current boom in generative AI, but he often discussed the possibility of machines eventually performing even highly skilled jobs, including making art. His point was that reducing the need for human labor should be something we celebrate. If machines can produce the things we need with less human effort, that should give people more freedom to enjoy their lives.

Instead, under the existing monetary system, we become more financially insecure. We gain the ability to produce more while working less, yet fear losing the wages that allow us to buy what is being produced. Fresco envisioned a society in which automation created widely shared abundance, improved everyone’s standard of living, and ultimately made the existing monetary system obsolete.

Technology can be our destroyer or our greatest liberator.  When technological advances are used to wage war, expand surveillance, or cut labor costs without protecting people’s livelihoods, it is understandable that people associate it with danger. Hollywood’s stories of machines turning against humanity reflect those anxieties. But a future in which technology threatens our survival is not inevitable. We just have to realize who the real bad guy is, and it's not AI.

Jacque Fresco is such a legend, I was just reading his book "The Best That Money Can't Buy - beyond politics, poverty and war" the other day, it's crazy how much of a visionaries he was, now that most of what he designed/imagined is what we are now dreaming of in a post scarcity world.

comments.author: hblok
comments.body:
Isn't this just another "Seize the means of production" idea, but in the future with "advanced technology" and AI?

The part that all collectivist systems fail to take into account is the individual. And some individuals do want to get ahead and have what others don't. Some want riches, status, power or prestige. Those are not going to change regardless of what socio-economic system you put on top.

Where capitalism has succeed over other systems, is that it has channeled that energy and drive into creation, development, science and arts that enriches many more than just the people who have worked for it and achieved it.

There are problems in the systems we have today. However, if the illusion is "AI will make universal basic income come true", then that is going to turn out pretty disappointing.
